methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $299M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Electra, a Series B climate and energy company founded by Sandeep Nijhawan and Quoc Pham, has raised $299M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 9 private and 1 public company in the Climate & Energy sector, including peers such as KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $299M total raised as a proxy for current value, applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $568M. Peer-median analysis examines three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: KoBold Metals at $3.0B (Series C), Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B (Series C), and Amogy at $700M (Series C). The peer median of $1.0B reflects the upper range of early-stage valuations in this capital-intensive sector, with a spread from $700M to $3.0B.

Triangulating these two methods produces a valuation range of $483M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $784M. The stage-progression method anchors the lower bound, while peer multiples—particularly the median—support higher valuations. Key uncertainties include technology de-risking timelines, which substantially influence peer valuations, and the representativeness of the three-company peer set in a rapidly evolving sector. The wide peer range ($700M–$3.0B) reflects heterogeneity in technology maturity and capital requirements across comparable companies.
